To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the baryons are able to make the inner DM density profile in dwarf galaxies shallower and that the ΛCDM simulations can explain the observed rotation curve shapes and the inner density slope of the DM density profiles of the THINGS dwarfs.

(1) the ΛCDM simulations of dwarf galaxies with baryonic feedback produce a stellar and baryon mass similar to that inferred for the THINGS dwarf galaxy sample from photometric and dynamical methods and (2) they also produce DM cores with a central logarithmic inner density profile slope similar to that of the THINGS galaxies.
the ΛCDM simulations of baryonic dwarf galaxies are able to form DM halos with the same mass distribution as that of the THINGS dwarfs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison between hydrodynamically simulated galaxies and the THINGS dwarf galaxy sample.
the question of how well the observed dwarf galaxies are reproduced in simulations of galaxy formation.
the question of whether or not the observed dwarf galaxy rotation curves are consistent with those predicted by the ΛCDM cosmological paradigm, and the answer is yes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the THINGS dwarf galaxy sample is consistent with ΛCDM, and the simulations presented here are able to explain the THINGS dwarf rotation curves.
the ΛCDM paradigm with its standard baryonic physics ingredients can account for the observed dark matter distribution in dwarf galaxies.
the ΛCDM cosmological model with the inclusion of baryonic effects can reproduce the observed dwarf galaxy rotation curves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ΛCDM cosmological model is consistent with the THINGS dwarf galaxy sample.
, if we take into account the baryonic effects, the ΛCDM cosmological model is consistent with the observed dark matter density profiles of dwarf galaxies.
the simulations are able to reproduce the observed rotation curves and density profiles of dwarf galaxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ΛCDM paradigm is able to account for the observed DM density profiles of dwarf galaxies without any need for ad hoc assumptions about the DM particle nature.
, in contrast to the common view, the ΛCDM cosmological paradigm does not predict a cusp/core dichotomy, but a continuous distribution of DM halo density profiles, with a wide range of inner slopes.

the ΛCDM paradigm can be reconciled with the observations of nearby dwarf galaxies if baryons play a key role in the formation of DM halos, which can be tested in the future with more detailed observations of nearby dwarf galaxy systems and with more sophisticated numerical simulations that include more physical processes.
